name: Fairmont The Palm Dubai
positioning: Beachfront resort hotel at the base of Dubai's Palm, with a range of rooms, family suites and apartments
best_for: Families who want family suites or apartments with kitchens
Travelers who want a beach resort with easier access to the rest of Dubai

facts.text: The hotel is set on the trunk of Dubai's Palm.
Being at the base of the Palm means easier access to the rest of Dubai than some competitors on the island.
The hotel has its own beach.
All rooms have large balconies with furniture.
Bathrooms have blue mosaics set against tan marble, deep tubs, separate showers and Le Labo toiletries.
One of the four pools is specifically for families.
Restaurants include a Brazilian steakhouse and Chinese fine dining.
Frevo is a Brazilian restaurant where meats are carved tableside in southern Brazilian style.
The Signature Jacuzzi Suite has a private balcony with a jacuzzi overlooking the Arabian Gulf.
Deluxe rooms have views of the Palm and the Dubai Marina skyline and a private balcony.

highlights.text: The Fairmont Serenity Room faces the Palm sea and includes access to the Thermal Oasis, a wellness breakfast by Zest served in the room and 30% off massages at Serenity Spa.
The Family 3 Bedroom Deluxe Palm Sea View Suite has three bedrooms, a walk-in wardrobe, marble bathrooms, a dining and lounge area and a kitchenette.
One and two bedroom apartments are located within the hotel, with a fully equipped kitchen and access to the gym, outdoor pools, private beach and kids club.
Fairmont Gold rooms and suites give access to the Fairmont Gold lounge, which has sea views and offers breakfast, afternoon tea, happy hour and evening canapés.

considerations.text: Rooms facing the road deal with traffic noise.
Wi-Fi in the rooms is expensive; it is free in public areas but does not reach the beach or pool areas.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Fairmont the Palm, Dubai
